suggestions.title: “since it's not "achieving something", but …”

suggestions.title: “A tightening won't tell you …”
suggestions.where: Let the response change the invitation, P1

edits.before: Your shoulders tightening, or 'hmm, that feels kind of wrong', is a signal to investigate further. A tightening won't tell you what it's about by itself, so ask what happened and whether the invitation fits. But 'No! That is Not Right!' is a signal to stop what you're doing and change it. If you don't feel like it fits, don't keep doing it, and don't try saying it again more persuasively. Just change it. You don't need any other reason.

suggestions.title: “Presumption is a powerful thing (a presupposition …”

edits.before: A presupposition is an assumption hidden inside a sentence. Presumption is a powerful thing, so please don’t use it except to presume that we will have the choice of when it will happen, that we will be able to do it, that we are safe, that we are loved and that our adult can lead us. Never use it to sneak in obedience.
edits.after: Presumption is a powerful thing (a presupposition hides an assumption inside a sentence, and the person hearing it usually takes that assumption on board), so please don’t use it except to presume that we will have the choice of when it will happen, that we will be able to do it, that we are safe, that we are loved and that our adult can lead us. Don’t ever presume obedience, the way a hypnotist does when they say something like, ‘As you go deeper, it gets easier and easier to just do what I say.’
